problemStatement.formal: \exists c > 0, \forall^{\text{f}} n, \forall P \text{ Littlewood of degree } n: \max_{|z|=1}|P(z)| > (1+c)\sqrt{n}
problemStatement.plain: Does there exist c > 0 such that for all large n and all ±1 coefficient polynomials of degree n, max_{|z|=1}|P(z)| > (1+c)√n?
whyMatters: Tests whether ±1 coefficients prevent ultraflat behavior on the unit circle
Connects polynomial analysis, harmonic analysis, and combinatorics

proven: Kahane (1980): ultraflat exist for unimodular coefficients (NOT ±1)
open: Does the (1+c)√n lower bound hold for ±1 polynomials?
What is inf of supNorm(P)/√n over degree-n Littlewood P?
Can the BBMST constant c₂ be made close to 1?
knownResults.goal: Formalize the conjecture and all known partial results

insights: IsLittlewoodPolynomial uses Polynomial ℂ with coefficient constraints — cleaner than custom structure
supNorm defined via ⨆ over unit circle — matches standard analysis conventions
Key gap: BBMST gives flat but not ultraflat; Kahane gives ultraflat but only for unimodular
The discreteness of {-1,+1} vs continuous {|z|=1} is the essential difficulty
Erdős #228 already had ErdosHaymanQuestion which is essentially #1150
Rudin-Shapiro gives concrete √2 upper bound ratio, establishing sup/√n can't diverge
mathlibGaps: No Parseval theorem for polynomials on unit circle in Mathlib
Limited sup norm theory for polynomials on compact sets
knowledge.markdown:
# Erdős #1150 - Knowledge Base

## Problem Statement

Does ∃ c > 0 such that ∀ large n, all degree-n ±1 polynomials have max_{|z|=1}|P(z)| > (1+c)√n?

## Status

**Erdős Database Status**: OPEN

## Formalization

- **File**: proofs/Proofs/Erdos1150Problem.lean
- **Sorries**: 1 (routine sup norm bound from BBMST)
- **Axioms**: 5 (Parseval, BBMST, Kahane, Rudin-Shapiro, equivalence)
- **Cross-references**: Erdős #228 (flat), #230 (unimodular ultraflat)

## Key Insight

Flat ≠ ultraflat. BBMST shows flat ±1 polynomials exist, Kahane shows ultraflat for unimodular. The gap (ultraflat for ±1?) is exactly Erdős #1150.
